questions.text: If for $\theta\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{3}, 0\right]$, the points $(x, y)=\left(3\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right), 2\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$ lie on $xy+\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $\phi=\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $t=\tan\phi=\dfrac{y}{2}$. Then $\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\phi+\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, so $\dfrac{x}{3}=\dfrac{t+\frac{1}{\sqrt3}}{1-\frac{t}{\sqrt3}}=\dfrac{\sqrt3\,t+1}{\sqrt3-t}$.
Hence $x(\sqrt3-t)=3(\sqrt3\,t+1)$; with $t=\dfrac y2$ and multiplying by 2: $xy-2\sqrt3\,x+3\sqrt3\,y+6=0$.
So $\alpha=-2\sqrt3$, $\beta=3\sqrt3$, $\gamma=6$ and $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=12+27+36=75$.

questions.text:
Among the statements
(S1) : The set $\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{-i\} : |z|=1 \text{ and } \dfrac{z-i}{z+i} \text{ is purely real}\right\}$ contains exactly two elements, and
(S2) : The set $\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{-1\} : |z|=1 \text{ and } \dfrac{z-1}{z+1} \text{ is purely imaginary}\right\}$ contains infinitely many elements.
questions.sol:
(S1): $\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}$ is real exactly when $z$, $i$, $-i$ are collinear, i.e. $z$ lies on the imaginary axis. On $|z|=1$ (with $z\ne-i$) this leaves only $z=i$, one element. (S1) is false.
(S2): for $z=e^{i\theta}$, $\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}=i\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, which is purely imaginary for every $z\ne\pm1$ on the circle: infinitely many elements. (S2) is true.

questions.text: Let the set of all values of $p\in\mathbb{R}$, for which both the roots of the equation $x^2-(p+2)x+(2p+9)=0$ are negative real numbers, be the interval $(\alpha, \beta]$. Then $\beta-2\alpha$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Real roots: $(p+2)^2-4(2p+9)=p^2-4p-32=(p-8)(p+4)\ge0$, so $p\le-4$ or $p\ge8$.
Both negative: sum $p+2<0$ and product $2p+9>0$, so $-\dfrac92<p<-2$.
Together $p\in\left(-\dfrac92, -4\right]$, so $\alpha=-\dfrac92$, $\beta=-4$ and $\beta-2\alpha=-4+9=5$.

questions.text:
Let the system of equations :
$2x+3y+5z=9$,
$7x+3y-2z=8$,
$12x+3y-(4+\lambda)z=16-\mu$,
have infinitely many solutions. Then the radius of the circle centred at $(\lambda, \mu)$ and touching the line $4x=3y$ is
questions.sol:
The $x$ and $y$ coefficients of the third equation are $-1\times$(first) $+\,2\times$(second): $-2+14=12$, $-3+6=3$.
For infinitely many solutions the whole third equation must be this combination: $z$: $-5-4=-9=-(4+\lambda)$, so $\lambda=5$; constants: $-9+16=7=16-\mu$, so $\mu=9$.
Radius $=$ distance of $(5, 9)$ from $4x-3y=0$ $=\dfrac{|20-27|}{5}=\dfrac75$.

questions.text:
Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $|\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A))|=81$. If
$S=\left\{n\in\mathbb{Z} : \left(|\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)|\right)^{\frac{(n-1)^2}{2}}=|A|^{(3n^2-5n-4)}\right\}$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{n\in S}\left|A^{(n^2+n)}\right|$ is equal to
questions.sol:
For a $3\times3$ matrix, $|\operatorname{adj}B|=|B|^2$, so $|\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A))|=|A|^8=81$, giving $|A|^2=3$.
$|\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)|=|A|^4$, so the condition is $|A|^{2(n-1)^2}=|A|^{3n^2-5n-4}$, i.e. $2n^2-4n+2=3n^2-5n-4$, i.e. $n^2-n-6=0$: $n=3$ or $n=-2$.
$\left|A^{n^2+n}\right|=|A|^{n^2+n}=3^{(n^2+n)/2}$: $n=3$ gives $3^6=729$, $n=-2$ gives $3^1=3$. Sum $=732$.

questions.text: Let $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ be in a geometric progression. If 2, 7, 9, 5 are subtracted respectively from $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$, then the resulting numbers are in an arithmetic progression. Then the value of $\dfrac{1}{24}(x_1x_2x_3x_4)$ is:
questions.sol:
Let the terms be $a, ar, ar^2, ar^3$. Equal differences of $a-2, ar-7, ar^2-9, ar^3-5$ give
$a(r-1)-5=ar(r-1)-2\Rightarrow a(r-1)^2=-3$ and $ar(r-1)-2=ar^2(r-1)+4\Rightarrow ar(r-1)^2=-6$.
Dividing, $r=2$ and $a=-3$: the terms are $-3, -6, -12, -24$.
$\dfrac{1}{24}(-3)(-6)(-12)(-24)=\dfrac{5184}{24}=216$.

questions.text: The remainder when $\left((64)^{(64)}\right)^{(64)}$ is divided by 7 is equal to
questions.sol:
$64=63+1\equiv1 \pmod 7$, so every power of 64 leaves remainder 1 on division by 7 (expand $(63+1)^k$ binomially: every term except the last is a multiple of 7).
Remainder $=1$.

questions.text: From a group of 7 batsmen and 6 bowlers, 10 players are to be chosen for a team, which should include atleast 4 batsmen and atleast 4 bowlers. One batsmen and one bowler who are captain and vice-captain respectively of the team should be included. Then the total number of ways such a selection can be made, is
questions.sol:
With the captain (a batsman) and vice-captain (a bowler) fixed, choose 8 more from 6 batsmen and 5 bowlers.
Team batsmen : bowlers can be 4 : 6, 5 : 5 or 6 : 4.
$4:6$: $\binom63\binom55=20$; $5:5$: $\binom64\binom54=75$; $6:4$: $\binom65\binom53=60$.
Total $=155$.

questions.text: Let P be the parabola, whose focus is $(-2, 1)$ and directrix is $2x+y+2=0$. Then the sum of the ordinates of the points on P, whose abscissa is $-2$, is
questions.sol:
For $(-2, y)$ on P: distance to focus $=|y-1|$, distance to directrix $=\dfrac{|-4+y+2|}{\sqrt5}=\dfrac{|y-2|}{\sqrt5}$.
$5(y-1)^2=(y-2)^2\Rightarrow 4y^2-6y+1=0$, whose roots are real.
Sum of the ordinates $=\dfrac64=\dfrac32$.

questions.text: Let ABC be the triangle such that the equations of lines AB and AC be $3y-x=2$ and $x+y=2$, respectively, and the points B and C lie on $x$-axis. If P is the orthocentre of the triangle ABC, then the area of the triangle PBC is equal to
questions.sol:
B: $y=0$ on $3y-x=2$ gives $B(-2, 0)$; C: $y=0$ on $x+y=2$ gives $C(2, 0)$; A $=(1, 1)$.
Altitude from A: $x=1$. Altitude from B (perpendicular to AC, slope 1): $y=x+2$. So $P=(1, 3)$.
Area of PBC $=\dfrac12\times4\times3=6$.

questions.text: Let $C_1$ be the circle in the third quadrant of radius 3, that touches both coordinate axes. Let $C_2$ be the circle with centre $(1, 3)$ that touches $C_1$ externally at the point $(\alpha, \beta)$. If $(\beta-\alpha)^2=\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$C_1$ has centre $(-3, -3)$ and radius 3. The distance between the centres is $\sqrt{4^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{13}$.
The point of contact lies on the line of centres at distance 3 from $(-3, -3)$: $(\alpha, \beta)=(-3, -3)+\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{13}}(4, 6)=\left(-3+\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{13}}, -3+\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{13}}\right)$.
$\beta-\alpha=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}$, so $(\beta-\alpha)^2=\dfrac{9}{13}$ and $m+n=22$.

questions.text: Let the line L pass through $(1, 1, 1)$ and intersect the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$. Then, which of the following points lies on the line L?
questions.sol:
General points: $(1+2s, -1+3s, 1+4s)$ and $(3+t, 4+2t, t)$. Their position vectors relative to $(1, 1, 1)$ are $(2s, 3s-2, 4s)$ and $(2+t, 3+2t, t-1)$, which must be parallel.
From the first and third components: $2s(t-1)=4s(2+t)\Rightarrow t=-5$, giving direction $(-3, -7, -6)$; then $s=-\dfrac65$ checks all ratios.
L: $(1, 1, 1)+k(3, 7, 6)$. With $k=2$ this gives $(7, 15, 13)$.

questions.text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y}{\alpha}=\dfrac{z-5}{1}$ is $\dfrac{5}{\sqrt6}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\alpha$ is
questions.sol:
Points $(1, 2, 3)$ and $(0, 0, 5)$, difference $(1, 2, -2)$; directions $(2, 3, 4)$ and $(1, \alpha, 1)$.
Cross product $=(3-4\alpha, 2, 2\alpha-3)$, with squared length $20\alpha^2-36\alpha+22$; dot product with $(1, 2, -2)$ is $13-8\alpha$.
$6(13-8\alpha)^2=25(20\alpha^2-36\alpha+22)\Rightarrow 116\alpha^2+348\alpha-464=0\Rightarrow \alpha^2+3\alpha-4=0$.
Sum of the values $=-3$.

questions.text: Let the angle $\theta$, $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ between two unit vectors $\hat a$ and $\hat b$ be $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{65}}{9}\right)$. If the vector $\vec c=3\hat a+6\hat b+9\left(\hat a\times\hat b\right)$, then the value of $9\left(\vec c\cdot\hat a\right)-3\left(\vec c\cdot\hat b\right)$ is
questions.sol:
$\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{65}{81}}=\dfrac49$, and $\hat a\times\hat b$ is perpendicular to both.
$\vec c\cdot\hat a=3+6\cdot\dfrac49=\dfrac{17}{3}$, $\vec c\cdot\hat b=3\cdot\dfrac49+6=\dfrac{22}{3}$.
$9\cdot\dfrac{17}{3}-3\cdot\dfrac{22}{3}=51-22=29$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\tan\left(5(x)^{\frac13}\right)\log_e\left(1+3x^2\right)}{\left(\tan^{-1}3\sqrt{x}\right)^2\left(e^{5(x)^{\frac43}}-1\right)}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Use $\tan u\sim u$, $\log_e(1+u)\sim u$, $\tan^{-1}u\sim u$, $e^u-1\sim u$ as $u\to0$.
Numerator $\sim 5x^{1/3}\cdot3x^2=15x^{7/3}$; denominator $\sim 9x\cdot5x^{4/3}=45x^{7/3}$.
Limit $=\dfrac{15}{45}=\dfrac13$.

questions.text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{(x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2x}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.sol:
With $x\to\pi-x$, $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{x\sin x}{1+3\cos^2x}dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2x}dx$.
Put $u=\cos x$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2x}dx=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{du}{1+3u^2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\sqrt3=\frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt3}$.
Integral $=\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}+3\right)\dfrac{2\pi}{3\sqrt3}=\dfrac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}(\pi+6)$.

questions.text: If the area of the region bounded by the curves $y=4-\dfrac{x^2}{4}$ and $y=\dfrac{x-4}{2}$ is equal to $\alpha$, then $6\alpha$ equals
questions.sol:
Intersections: $16-x^2=2x-8\Rightarrow x^2+2x-24=0$, so $x=-6, 4$.
$\alpha=\displaystyle\int_{-6}^{4}\left(6-\frac x2-\frac{x^2}{4}\right)dx=\left[6x-\frac{x^2}{4}-\frac{x^3}{12}\right]_{-6}^{4}=\frac{44}{3}+27=\frac{125}{3}$.
$6\alpha=250$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $x\left(x^2+e^x\right)dy+\left(e^x(x-2)y-x^3\right)dx=0$, $x>0$, passing through the point $(1, 0)$. Then $y(2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{e^x(x-2)}{x(x^2+e^x)}y=\dfrac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}$, a linear equation.
With $g(x)=\dfrac{x^2+e^x}{x^2}=1+\dfrac{e^x}{x^2}$, $\dfrac{g^\prime}{g}=\dfrac{e^x(x-2)}{x^3}\cdot\dfrac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}$, so $g$ is an integrating factor.
$y\,g=\displaystyle\int1\,dx=x+C$; $(1, 0)$ gives $C=-1$. So $y=\dfrac{x^2(x-1)}{x^2+e^x}$ and $y(2)=\dfrac{4}{4+e^2}$.

questions.text: For $n\ge2$, let $S_n$ denote the set of all subsets of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ with no two consecutive numbers. For example $\{1, 3, 5\}\in S_6$, but $\{1, 2, 4\}\notin S_6$. Then $n(S_5)$ is equal to ______
questions.sol:
Let $a_n=n(S_n)$, counting the empty set. A subset either omits $n$ (giving $a_{n-1}$ choices) or contains $n$ and omits $n-1$ (giving $a_{n-2}$).
$a_1=2$, $a_2=3$, so $a_3=5$, $a_4=8$, $a_5=13$.

questions.text: The number of singular matrices of order 2, whose elements are from the set $\{2, 3, 6, 9\}$, is ______.
questions.sol:
$\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$ is singular when $ad=bc$. Count ordered pairs by product:
4: 1, 6: 2, 9: 1, 12: 2, 18: 4 ($2\cdot9$, $9\cdot2$, $3\cdot6$, $6\cdot3$), 27: 2, 36: 1, 54: 2, 81: 1.
Number of matrices $=\sum(\text{count})^2=1+4+1+4+16+4+1+4+1=36$.

questions.text: Consider the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ having one of its focus at $P(-3, 0)$. If the latus ractum through its other focus subtends a right angle at P and $a^2b^2=\alpha\sqrt2-\beta$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
questions.sol:
$a^2+b^2=9$. The other focus is $S(3, 0)$ and the latus rectum ends are $\left(3, \pm\dfrac{b^2}{a}\right)$.
A right angle at P with $PS=6$ means each half subtends $45^\circ$: $\dfrac{b^2}{a}=6$.
$a^2+6a-9=0\Rightarrow a=3\sqrt2-3$, and $a^2b^2=6a^3=6\cdot27(\sqrt2-1)^3=162(5\sqrt2-7)=810\sqrt2-1134$.
$\alpha+\beta=810+1134=1944$.

questions.text: The number of relations on the set $A=\{1, 2, 3\}$, containing at most 6 elements including $(1, 2)$, which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is ______
questions.sol:
Reflexivity needs $(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)$; with $(1, 2)$ that is 4 elements, so at most 2 more pairs from $(2,1), (1,3), (3,1), (2,3), (3,2)$.
No extra pair: transitive, not symmetric (1 relation).
One extra: $(1,3)$ or $(3,2)$ work; $(2,1)$ makes it symmetric; $(3,1)$ and $(2,3)$ break transitivity (2 relations).
Two extra: only $\{(1,3), (2,3)\}$, $\{(1,3), (3,2)\}$ and $\{(3,1), (3,2)\}$ keep transitivity (3 relations).
Total $=6$.

questions.text: The number of points of discontinuity of the function $f(x)=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]-\left[\sqrt x\right]$, $x\in[0, 4]$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is ______
questions.sol:
$\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]$ jumps where $x^2=2k$: $x=\sqrt2, 2, \sqrt6, \sqrt8, \sqrt{10}, \sqrt{12}, \sqrt{14}, 4$. $[\sqrt x]$ jumps at $x=1$ and $x=4$.
At $x=4$ both jump by 1, so $f(4^-)=7-1=6=f(4)$: continuous. At $x=0$ $f$ is right-continuous.
Discontinuities: $1, \sqrt2, 2, \sqrt6, \sqrt8, \sqrt{10}, \sqrt{12}, \sqrt{14}$, i.e. 8 points.

questions.text: If $\epsilon_0$ denotes the permittivity of free space and $\Phi_E$ is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then dimensions of $\left(\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}\right)$ are that of :
questions.sol: By Gauss's law $\epsilon_0\Phi_E$ has the dimensions of charge, so $\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ has the dimensions of charge per unit time, i.e. electric current (it is the displacement current).

questions.text: Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths 30 cm and 10 cm are placed coaxially, 10 cm apart. The power of this combination is:
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1F=\dfrac1{f_1}+\dfrac1{f_2}-\dfrac{d}{f_1f_2}=\dfrac1{30}+\dfrac1{10}-\dfrac{10}{300}=\dfrac{1}{10}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$.
$F=10$ cm $=0.1$ m, so $P=10$ D.

questions.text: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $\vec F=\left(2t\,\hat i+3t^2\,\hat j\right)$ N. The power generated by the force at time t is:
questions.sol:
With $m=1$ kg, $\vec a=2t\,\hat i+3t^2\,\hat j$; taking the object to start from rest at $t=0$, $\vec v=t^2\,\hat i+t^3\,\hat j$.
$P=\vec F\cdot\vec v=2t\cdot t^2+3t^2\cdot t^3=(2t^3+3t^5)$ W.

questions.text:
A rod of length 5 L is bent right angle keeping one side length as 2 L.
The position of the centre of mass of the system:
(Consider L = 10 cm)
questions.sol:
The uniform rod splits into a 3L piece along the $y$-axis (mass $\frac35M$, centre at $(0, 1.5L)$) and a 2L piece along the $x$-axis (mass $\frac25M$, centre at $(L, 0)$).
$x_{cm}=\dfrac25L=4$ cm, $y_{cm}=\dfrac35(1.5L)=0.9L=9$ cm.
Centre of mass $=4\hat i+9\hat j$ (in cm).

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles $(45^\circ+\alpha)$ and $(45^\circ-\alpha)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.sol: $T=\dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$, so $\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}=\dfrac{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}{\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)}=\dfrac{\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha}=\dfrac{1+\tan\alpha}{1-\tan\alpha}$.

questions.text: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths $\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}=\dfrac13$ and their diameters ratio $\dfrac{d_A}{d_B}=2$. If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations ?
questions.sol:
$\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}\propto\dfrac{L}{d^2}$ for the same force and material.
$\dfrac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B}=\dfrac13\times\left(\dfrac12\right)^2=\dfrac1{12}$, i.e. 1 : 12.

questions.text: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave $x=a\cos(1.5t)\cos(50.5t)$ where t is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat. (close to nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$2\cos A\cos B=\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)$: the two components have angular frequencies $52$ and $49$ rad/s.
Beat angular frequency $=52-49=3$ rad/s, so the beat period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\approx2.09$ s, i.e. about 2 s.

questions.text:
An ac current is represented as
$i=5\sqrt2+10\cos\left(650\pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ Amp
The r.m.s value of the current is
questions.sol:
The mean of $i^2$ over a period is $(5\sqrt2)^2+\dfrac{10^2}{2}=50+50=100$ (the cross term averages to zero).
$i_{rms}=\sqrt{100}=10$ A.

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is bent into a triangular pyramid as shown in figure with each segment having same length. The resistance between points A and B is R/n. The value of n is :
questions.sol:
The six equal edges each have resistance $r=\dfrac R6$.
Between A and B, the other two vertices are at the same potential by symmetry, so the edge joining them carries no current. What remains is $r$ (edge AB) in parallel with two paths of $2r$ each: $\dfrac{1}{R_{AB}}=\dfrac1r+\dfrac1{2r}+\dfrac1{2r}=\dfrac2r$.
$R_{AB}=\dfrac r2=\dfrac R{12}$, so $n=12$.

questions.text: A particle of charge q, mass m and kinetic energy E enters in magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity and undergoes a circular arc of radius (r). Which of the following curves represents the variation of r with E?
questions.sol:
$r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB}\propto\sqrt E$.
So $r$ rises from the origin with decreasing slope: the concave-down curve of option (1).

questions.text: Two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated by a distance of 30 cm. A third charge $q_3$ initially at 'C' as shown in the figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40 cm from C to D. If the difference in potential energy due to movement of $q_3$ from C to D is given by $\dfrac{q_3K}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$, the value of K is:
questions.sol:
$q_1$ is at the centre A of the circle, so its contribution does not change.
From $q_2$: distance at C $=\sqrt{0.3^2+0.4^2}=0.5$ m, at D $=0.4-0.3=0.1$ m.
$\Delta U=\dfrac{q_2q_3}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac1{0.1}-\dfrac1{0.5}\right)=\dfrac{q_3(8q_2)}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$, so $K=8q_2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The percentage increase in magnetic field (B) when space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium (magnetic susceptibility $\chi_{\text{Mg}}=1.2\times10^{-5}$) is :
questions.sol:
$B=\mu_0(1+\chi)nI$, so the fractional increase is $\chi=1.2\times10^{-5}$.
Percentage increase $=1.2\times10^{-3}\%=\dfrac65\times10^{-3}\%$.

questions.text:
Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths ($B_1$ and $B_2$), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass m and charge q, at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocity v and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface ?
(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and $B_2>B_1$)
questions.sol:
Entering perpendicular to the interface, the particle describes a semicircle in each region; both fields point the same way, so it keeps turning in the same sense.
In region 2 it shifts by $2r_2=\dfrac{2mv}{qB_2}$ along the interface, and in region 1 by $2r_1=\dfrac{2mv}{qB_1}$ in the opposite direction.
Net displacement $=2r_1-2r_2=\dfrac{mv}{qB_1}\left(1-\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}\right)\times2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are
$E_1=E_0\,\text{Sin}\,\omega t$
$E_2=E_0\,\text{Sin}\left(\omega t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$
Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
questions.sol: Resultant amplitude $=\sqrt{E_0^2+E_0^2+2E_0^2\cos\frac{\pi}{3}}=\sqrt3\,E_0\approx1.7\,E_0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length of 12 cm, when it is in air. Find the focal length of the lens when it is placed in water.
(Take refractive index of water as 1.28)
questions.sol:
By the lens maker's formula, $\dfrac{f_w}{f_a}=\dfrac{\mu-1}{\frac{\mu}{\mu_w}-1}=\dfrac{0.6}{1.25-1}=2.4$.
$f_w=2.4\times12=28.8$ cm $=288$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For a hydrogen atom, the ratio of the largest wavelength of Lyman series to that of the Balmer series is
questions.sol:
Lyman, longest ($2\to1$): $\dfrac1\lambda=R\left(1-\dfrac14\right)=\dfrac{3R}{4}$. Balmer, longest ($3\to2$): $\dfrac1\lambda=R\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac{5R}{36}$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{4/3}{36/5}=\dfrac{5}{27}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a hydrogen like ion, the energy difference between the $2^{\text{nd}}$ excitation energy state and ground is 108.8 eV. The atomic number of the ion is:
questions.sol:
The second excited state is $n=3$: $\Delta E=13.6Z^2\left(1-\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac{108.8}{9}Z^2$ eV.
$\dfrac{108.8}{9}Z^2=108.8\Rightarrow Z=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In the following circuit, the reading of the ammeter will be
(Take Zener breakdown voltage = 4 V)
questions.sol:
Without the Zener diode the 400 $\Omega$ resistor would get $12\times\dfrac{400}{500}=9.6$ V $>4$ V, so the Zener diode is in breakdown and holds 4 V across the parallel branches.
Ammeter current (through 400 $\Omega$) $=\dfrac{4}{400}$ A $=10$ mA.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A, B and C are disc, solid sphere and spherical shell respectively with same radii and masses. These masses are placed as shown in figure.
The moment of inertia of the given system about PQ axis is $\dfrac{x}{15}$I, where I is the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Disc A: PQ is a diameter, $I_A=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}=I$.
Sphere B and shell C have their centres at distance $R$ from PQ: $I_B=\dfrac25MR^2+MR^2=\dfrac75MR^2$, $I_C=\dfrac23MR^2+MR^2=\dfrac53MR^2$.
Total $=MR^2\left(\dfrac14+\dfrac75+\dfrac53\right)=\dfrac{199}{60}MR^2=\dfrac{199}{15}I$, so $x=199$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
A wire of length 10 cm and diameter 0.5 mm is used in a bulb. The temperature of the wire is 1727$^\circ$C and power radiated by the wire is 94.2 W. Its emissivity is $\dfrac x8$ where $x$ = ______.
(Given $\sigma=6.0\times10^{-8}$ W m$^{-2}$ K$^{-4}$, $\pi=3.14$ and assume that the emissivity of wire material is same at all wavelength.)
questions.sol:
Radiating area (curved surface) $A=\pi dL=3.14\times0.5\times10^{-3}\times0.1=1.57\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$; $T=2000$ K, $T^4=1.6\times10^{13}$ K$^4$.
$P=e\sigma AT^4=e\times6.0\times10^{-8}\times1.57\times10^{-4}\times1.6\times10^{13}=150.72\,e$ W.
$e=\dfrac{94.2}{150.72}=0.625=\dfrac58$, so $x=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An ideal gas has undergone through the cyclic process as shown in the figure. Work done by the gas in the entire cycle is ______ $\times10^{-1}$ J.
(Take $\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
The work in a cycle equals the area enclosed on the P-V diagram. The circle has semi-axes $100$ kPa and $100$ cm$^3$.
Area $=\pi\times(100\times10^3)\times(100\times10^{-6})=3.14\times10=31.4$ J $=314\times10^{-1}$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For ac circuit shown in figure, R = 100 k$\Omega$ and C = 100 pF and the phase difference between $V_{in}$ and $(V_B-V_A)$ is $90^\circ$. The input signal frequency is $10^x$ rad/sec, where '$x$' is ______.
questions.sol:
Each branch divides $V_{in}$: $V_A$ is the drop across C in the R-C branch and $V_B$ the drop across R in the C-R branch. With $X=\dfrac1{\omega C}$,
$V_B-V_A=V_{in}\dfrac{R+jX}{R-jX}$, which has the same magnitude as $V_{in}$ and leads it by $2\tan^{-1}\dfrac XR$.
A $90^\circ$ difference needs $X=R$: $\omega=\dfrac1{RC}=\dfrac1{10^5\times10^{-10}}=10^5$ rad/s, so $x=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height H above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm. The value of H is ______ cm. (Consider liquids are immisible)
questions.sol:
Shift $=t_1\left(1-\dfrac1{\mu_1}\right)+t_2\left(1-\dfrac1{\mu_2}\right)=60\left(1-\dfrac1{1.2}\right)+H\left(1-\dfrac1{1.6}\right)=10+\dfrac{3H}{8}$.
$10+\dfrac{3H}{8}=40\Rightarrow H=80$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas: 70.0, oxygen gas: 27.0 and argon gas: 3.0. If total pressure is 1.15 atm, then calculate the ratio of following respectively:
(i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas
(ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas
(Given: Molar mass of N, O and Ar are 14, 16 and 40 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)
questions.sol:
Partial pressures are in the ratio of moles. In 100 g: $\mathrm{N_2}$ $\dfrac{70}{28}=2.5$ mol, $\mathrm{O_2}$ $\dfrac{27}{32}=0.844$ mol, Ar $\dfrac{3}{40}=0.075$ mol.
(i) $\dfrac{2.5}{0.844}=2.96$; (ii) $\dfrac{0.844}{0.075}=11.25\approx11.2$. (The total pressure is not needed for the ratios.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct, if the threshold frequency of caesium is $5.16\times10^{14}$ Hz?
A. When Cs is placed inside a vacuum chamber with an ammeter connected to it and yellow light is focused on Cs, the ammeter shows the presence of current.
B. When the brightness of the yellow light is dimmed, the value of the current in the ammeter is reduced.
C. When a red light is used instead of the yellow light, the current produced is higher with respect to the yellow light.
D. When a blue light is used, the ammeter shows the formation of current.
E. When a white light is used. the ammeter shows formation of current.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E Only
A, B, D and E Only
questions.sol:
Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0=\dfrac{c}{\nu_0}=\dfrac{3\times10^8}{5.16\times10^{14}}\approx581$ nm.
Yellow (shorter than about 580 nm on the given spectrum), blue and white light all contain wavelengths below $\lambda_0$, so A, D and E are correct. Dimmer light means fewer photons and a smaller current (B correct). Red light ($\lambda>\lambda_0$) emits no electrons (C wrong).
A, B, D and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Total enthalpy change for freezing of 1 mol of water at 10$^\circ$C to ice at $-10^\circ$C is ______
(Given: $\Delta_{\text{fus}}H=x$ kJ/mol
$C_p[\mathrm{H_2O(l)}]=y$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
$C_p[\mathrm{H_2O(s)}]=z$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
In joules: cooling the water from 10$^\circ$C to 0$^\circ$C gives $-10y$; freezing gives $-1000x$; cooling the ice from 0$^\circ$C to $-10^\circ$C gives $-10z$.
Total $=-1000x-10y-10z=-10(100x+y+z)$ J.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An aqueous solution of HCl with pH 1.0 is diluted by adding equal volume of water (ignoring dissociation of water). The pH of HCl solution would
(Given log 2 = 0.30)
questions.sol:
$[\mathrm{H^+}]$ falls from 0.1 M to 0.05 M.
pH $=-\log(5\times10^{-2})=2-\log5=1+\log2=1.3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mohr's salt is composed of only three types of ions-ferrous, ammonium and sulfate.
Statement II: If the molar conductance at infinite dilution for ferrous, ammonium and sulfate ions are $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, respectively then the molar conductance for Mohr's salt solution at infinite dilution would be given by $x_1+x_2+2x_3$
In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statements I and Statement II are true
Both Statements I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Mohr's salt, $\mathrm{FeSO_4\cdot(NH_4)_2SO_4\cdot6H_2O}$, gives only $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions: Statement I is true.
By Kohlrausch's law, one formula unit gives 1 $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, 2 $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and 2 $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$, so $\Lambda_m^\circ=x_1+2x_2+2x_3$: Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Reaction $\mathrm{A(g)\rightarrow2B(g)+C(g)}$ is a first order reaction. It was started with pure A
t/minPressure of system at time t/mm Hg
10160
$\infty$240
Which of the following option is incorrect?
options: Initial pressure of A is 80 mm Hg
Partial pressure of A after 10 minute is 40 mm Hg
Rate constant of the reaction is 1.693 min$^{-1}$
The reaction never goes to completion
questions.sol:
At completion the pressure is $3p_0=240$, so $p_0=80$ mm Hg. At 10 min, $p_0+2x=160$ gives $x=40$, so $p_A=40$ mm Hg.
Half of A reacts in 10 min, so $t_{1/2}=10$ min and $k=\dfrac{0.693}{10}=0.0693$ min$^{-1}$, not 1.693 min$^{-1}$.
A first-order reaction only approaches completion asymptotically, so statements (1), (2) and (4) hold; (3) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacterial growth started to happen at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay(r) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine?
[Given: N = No. of bacteria, t = time, bacterial growth follows 1$^{\text{st}}$ order kinetics.]
questions.sol:
Before: first-order growth, $N=N_0e^{kt}$, so $\dfrac{N}{N_0}$ starts at 1 and rises exponentially.
After: $r=k^\prime N^2$, a parabola through the origin in the r-N graph.
Only option (4) shows both.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-I
LIST-I
Molecule / ion		LIST-II
Bond pair : lone pair
(on the central atom)
A. $\mathrm{ICl_2^-}$I. 4 : 2
B. $\mathrm{H_2O}$II. 4 : 1
C. $\mathrm{SO_2}$III. 2 : 3
D. $\mathrm{XeF_4}$IV. 2 : 2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{ICl_2^-}$: 2 bond pairs, 3 lone pairs (III). $\mathrm{H_2O}$: 2 : 2 (IV). $\mathrm{SO_2}$: two S=O double bonds count as 4 bond pairs, with 1 lone pair (II). $\mathrm{XeF_4}$: 4 : 2 (I).
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of valence electrons present in the metal among Cr, Co, Fe and Ni which has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation is
questions.sol:
Enthalpies of atomisation (kJ mol$^{-1}$): Cr 397, Fe 416, Co 425, Ni 430. Chromium is lowest.
Cr is $3d^54s^1$: 6 valence electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The group 14 elements A and B have the first ionisation enthalpy values of 708 and 715 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. The above values are lowest among their group members. The nature of their ions $\mathrm{A^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{B^{4+}}$ respectively is
questions.sol:
The two lowest first ionisation enthalpies in group 14 are those of Sn (708) and Pb (715 kJ mol$^{-1}$), so A = Sn and B = Pb.
By the inert pair effect, +4 is the stable state of Sn and +2 that of Pb. So $\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}$ tends to be oxidised (a reducing agent) and $\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}$ tends to be reduced (an oxidising agent).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The first transition series metal 'M' has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in its series. One of its aquated ion $(\mathrm{M^{n+}})$ exists in green colour. The nature of the oxide formed by the above $\mathrm{M^{n+}}$ ion is:
questions.sol:
Vanadium has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in the 3d series. Its green aquated ion is $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$.
The corresponding oxide $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$ is basic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An octahedral complex having molecular composition $\mathrm{Co.5NH_3.Cl.SO_4}$ has two isomers A and B. The solution of A gives a white precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution and the solution of B gives white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ solution. The type of isomerism exhibited by the complex is,
questions.sol:
A is $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5SO_4]Cl}$ (free $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ gives AgCl) and B is $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]SO_4}$ (free $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ gives $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$).
The isomers give different ions in solution: ionisation isomerism.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: When a salt is treated with sodium hydroxide solution it gives gas X. On passing gas X through reagent Y a brown coloured precipitate is formed. X and Y respectively, are
questions.sol:
An ammonium salt heated with NaOH gives ammonia gas (X = $\mathrm{NH_3}$).
Ammonia with Nessler's reagent (alkaline $\mathrm{K_2HgI_4}$) gives a brown precipitate (iodide of Millon's base). So Y = $\mathrm{K_2HgI_4}$ + KOH.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Dimethyl ether is completely soluble in water. However, diethyl ether is soluble in water to a very small extent.
Statement II: Sodium metal can be used to dry diethyl ether and not ethyl alcohol.
In the light of given statements. choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
questions.sol:
Statement I: dimethyl ether is miscible with water (hydrogen bonding with a small alkyl part), while diethyl ether dissolves only slightly. True.
Statement II: sodium does not react with ethers, so it can dry diethyl ether, but it reacts with ethanol (giving sodium ethoxide and $\mathrm{H_2}$). True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of given organic compound (X)?
questions.sol:
X is $\mathrm{CH_3CH=C(CH_3)CH_2Br}$. The parent chain has four carbons with the double bond at C-2 from either end; numbering from the $\mathrm{CH_2Br}$ end gives the substituents the lower locants (Br at 1, methyl at 2).
Name: 1-Bromo-2-methylbut-2-ene.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
The reactions which cannot be applied to prepare an alkene by elimination, are
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: a secondary bromide with the strong base NaOEt undergoes dehydrohalogenation, giving an alkene.
B: aqueous KOH with 2-bromobutane mainly gives the alcohol by substitution (alcoholic KOH is needed for elimination).
C: tert-butyl bromide with NaOMe eliminates to 2-methylpropene.
D: phenol with acidified dichromate is oxidised (to benzoquinone), not converted into an alkene.
E: a tertiary alcohol over Cu at 573 K is dehydrated to 2-methylpropene.
So B and D cannot be used.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ of cis-2-butene gives ethanal.
Statement II: The product obtained by ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ of 3, 6-dimethyloct-4-ene has no chiral carbon atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH_3}$ gives two molecules of $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ (ethanal). True.
Statement II: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH=CHCH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3}$ gives two molecules of $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CHO}$ (2-methylbutanal), whose C-2 carries H, $\mathrm{CH_3}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_5}$ and CHO: a chiral carbon. False.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is least likely to give effervescence of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ in presence of aq. $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ ?
questions.sol:
Only acids stronger than carbonic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_a\approx6.4$) release $\mathrm{CO_2}$ from $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$.
4-Nitrobenzoic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_a\approx3.4$), anilinium chloride ($\mathrm{p}K_a\approx4.6$) and picric acid ($\mathrm{p}K_a\approx0.4$) do; 3-nitrophenol ($\mathrm{p}K_a\approx8.4$) does not, because a meta nitro group cannot stabilise the phenoxide by resonance.
Answer: 3-nitrophenol, option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following amine (s) show (s) positive carbylamine test?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is given only by primary amines.
A (aniline) and C ($\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$) are primary; B and E are secondary and D is tertiary.
A and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: D-(+)-glucose + D-(+) fructose $\xrightarrow{-\mathrm{H_2O}}$ Sucrose
sucrose $\xrightarrow{\text{hydrolysis}}$ D-(+) glucose + D -(+) fructose
Statement II: Invert sugar is formed during sucrose hydrolysis
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
questions.sol:
Statement I: the fructose involved is D-($-$)-fructose (laevorotatory), not D-(+)-fructose. False.
Statement II: hydrolysis turns dextrorotatory sucrose into a laevorotatory mixture of glucose and fructose, called invert sugar. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
1 Faraday electricity was passed through $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ (1.5 M, 1 L) /Cu and 0.1 Faraday was passed through $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ (0.2 M, 1 L)/Ag electrolytic cells. After this the two cells were connected as shown below to make an electrochemical cell. The emf of the cell thus formed at 298 K is ______ mV (nearest integer)
Given : $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}}=0.34$ V
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}=0.8$ V
$\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.06$ V
questions.sol:
1 F deposits 0.5 mol Cu, leaving $[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}]=1.0$ M; 0.1 F deposits 0.1 mol Ag, leaving $[\mathrm{Ag^+}]=0.1$ M.
Cell $\mathrm{Cu|Cu^{2+}(1\,M)||Ag^+(0.1\,M)|Ag}$: $E^\circ=0.80-0.34=0.46$ V, $n=2$.
$E=0.46-\dfrac{0.06}{2}\log\dfrac{1}{(0.1)^2}=0.46-0.06=0.40$ V $=400$ mV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The percentage dissociation of a salt $(\mathrm{MX_3})$ solution at given temperature (van't Hoff factor i = 2) is ______ %(Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{MX_3}\rightarrow\mathrm{M^{3+}}+3\mathrm{X^-}$ gives 4 ions, so $i=1+3\alpha=2$.
$\alpha=\dfrac13$, i.e. about 33%.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of paramagnetic complexes among $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$, and $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, which involved $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is ______
questions.sol:
Inner-orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complexes form with strong-field ligands: $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^5$, 1 unpaired electron), $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^4$, 2 unpaired) and $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ ($d^6$, none, diamagnetic).
The fluoride and chloride complexes are high-spin $sp^3d^2$.
Paramagnetic and $d^2sp^3$: 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An organic compound weighing 500 mg, produced 220 mg of $\mathrm{CO_2}$, on complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon in the compound is ______%. (nearest integer)
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of C:12, O:16)
questions.sol:
Mass of carbon $=\dfrac{12}{44}\times220=60$ mg.
Percentage of carbon $=\dfrac{60}{500}\times100=12\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Thyroxine, the hormone has given below structure
The percentage of iodine in thyroxine is ______%. (nearest integer)
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C:12, H:1, O:16, N:14, I:127)
questions.sol:
Thyroxine is $\mathrm{C_{15}H_{11}I_4NO_4}$: $M=180+11+508+14+64=777$ g mol$^{-1}$.
Percentage of iodine $=\dfrac{508}{777}\times100=65.4\approx65\%$.
